Eligible Unused Period is the portion of the billing period not consumed at the point the prorated refund applies, measured in days
Taxes are not included in the Eligible Charge unless a policy or agreement says otherwise
Rounding is to two decimal places

query: When you work out proration, how many days do you count a monthly billing period as?
expected_intent: state the calculation assumption of 30 days for a monthly period and 365 days for annual
required_facts: A monthly billing period is treated as 30 days
An annual billing period is treated as 365 days
Day counts run from the start of the billing period to the effective date of the refund, inclusive of the start date

query: Does cancelling my plan automatically give me a prorated refund for the rest of the month?
expected_intent: state that prorated refunds are the exception and cancellation alone creates none
required_facts: Proration is the exception, not the default
Unused time is not automatically refundable unless a policy explicitly permits it
Cancelling a subscription does not create a prorated refund on its own

query: My request is outside the 30-day window. Is there any way to get a refund anyway?
expected_intent: explain that requests after the window closes may only proceed through the Refund Exception Approval policy
required_facts: Refunds outside the standard policy require exception approval
Customer Support agents cannot issue such a refund on their own
Approval of one exception does not entitle the customer to a repeat exception

query: Who is allowed to approve a refund that isn't covered by the standard policy?
expected_intent: identify the appropriate approver for refund exceptions
required_facts: Exceptions must be approved by the appropriate approver, typically a Billing Operations manager
Higher-value exceptions and exceptions involving an Enterprise account are escalated per Billing Operations procedures
Approved exceptions are recorded in the customer's billing record with the approval and reason

query: What is a goodwill credit and how does AcmeFlow give one out?
expected_intent: explain goodwill credits granted for service or billing issues and how they are held
required_facts: Goodwill credits are granted for service or billing issues
Goodwill grants require appropriate approval, typically a Billing Operations manager
Goodwill amounts are determined case by case and are not a published schedule
An approved goodwill credit is held as a workspace credit balance

query: When you refund me, does the money go back to my card or as a credit on my account?
expected_intent: explain refunds return to the original payment method or become a workspace credit balance
required_facts: An eligible refund is returned to the original payment method where AcmeFlow can do so
When a refund is issued as credit, or the original payment method is no longer available, the amount is held as a workspace credit balance
Credit balances are applied automatically to future invoices in order of invoice generation

query: Can I withdraw the credit balance on my workspace as cash?
expected_intent: state that credit balances have no cash-out value
required_facts: Credits have no cash-out value
Credit balances cannot be withdrawn, transferred, or exchanged for money back
A credit balance is not exchangeable for a refund

query: What happens to my remaining credit balance if I cancel my subscription?
expected_intent: explain credit balances are forfeited on cancellation unless a contract says otherwise
required_facts: If a subscription is cancelled, any remaining credit balance is forfeited unless a contract says otherwise
Unused credit cannot be carried beyond the agreement's terms
Customers who plan to cancel should be told this before cancelling

query: Roughly how long does a refund to a credit card take to show up?
expected_intent: provide the card refund timeframe of 5-10 business days
required_facts: Credit and debit card refunds typically take 5-10 business days to appear
The timeframe depends on the card issuer
Timeframes are estimates, not guarantees

query: How long do PayPal refunds usually take?
expected_intent: provide the PayPal refund timeframe of 5-7 business days
required_facts: PayPal refunds typically take 5-7 business days
Timing is counted in business days from the date AcmeFlow processes the refund
Timeframes are estimates and may vary

query: When does the refund timing actually start counting from?
expected_intent: explain refund timeframes start from when AcmeFlow processes the refund, in business days
required_facts: Timeframes count in business days from the date the refund is processed by AcmeFlow
They do not count from the date the request was submitted
A refund may appear sooner or later than the estimate depending on the financial institutions involved

query: If I remove seats from my Pro workspace, will I get any money back for them?
expected_intent: state that removing seats affects future billing only and creates no partial refund
required_facts: Removing seats normally affects future billing only
Unused time for removed seats is not automatically refunded
The default position is that most seat and plan changes affect future billing only

query: Does downgrading my plan trigger a partial refund for the time I won't use?
expected_intent: state that a downgrade takes effect next cycle and does not create a partial refund
required_facts: A plan downgrade takes effect at the start of the next billing cycle
Unused time in the current cycle is not automatically refunded unless a policy explicitly allows it
Cancelling also does not automatically create a partial refund

query: In which situations can a partial refund actually be issued?
expected_intent: list the specific situations where a partial refund may apply
required_facts: A prorated refund explicitly permitted by an applicable policy or signed agreement, refunding only part of a charge
An exception covering a partial amount approved under the Refund Exception Approval policy
A signed Enterprise agreement that provides for a partial refund in a defined situation
Partial amounts use the prorated refund formula unless the agreement defines its own calculation
